title: Finite diagrams in core homotopy fibers contract under right approximation
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent limits, cores, internal functor simplicial sets, Kan complexes and homotopy fibers of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $A,B$ be quasicategories in a common sufficiently large universe, both admitting limits indexed by every simplicial set with finitely many nondegenerate simplices, and let $G:A\to B$ preserve those limits. Assume that $G$ reflects equivalence edges. Assume also right approximation: for every $a\in A$, $b\in B$ and edge $\psi:b\to G(a)$ there exist an edge $v:a'\to a$ in $A$ and an equivalence $e:b\to G(a')$ such that $[G(v)e]=[\psi]$ in $hB$, whose morphism sets are $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_B(-,-)$. For $b\in B$ put
$$P_b=A^\simeq\times_{B^\simeq,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B^\simeq)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B^\simeq}\{b\}.$$
Then $P_b$ has a vertex, and for every finite simplicial set $K$ and simplicial map $f:K\to P_b$ there are a vertex $p\in P_b$ and a simplicial homotopy $H:K\times\Delta^1\to P_b$ from the constant map at $p$ to $f$ (either endpoint orientation is allowed). The assertion includes $K=\varnothing$.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7 and its proof, printed pp. 387-388, specialized to invertible weak equivalences and actual finite coherent limits; agent expansion from finite poset nerves to finite simplicial shapes using their assumed limits; read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $A^\simeq$ and $B^\simeq$ are Kan complexes. Apply [lem-coef-kan-fiber-path-reversal] to $G^\simeq:A^\simeq\to B^\simeq$. Besides the displayed $P_b$, this gives the Kan complex $Q_b=\{b\}\times_{B^\simeq,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B^\simeq)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B^\simeq}A^\simeq$ and simplicial maps $R:P_b\to Q_b$, $S:Q_b\to P_b$ with $SR\simeq\operatorname{id}_{P_b}$. It suffices to contract finite diagrams in $Q_b$; step 7 will transport the actual homotopy back, including its specified endpoint.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, proof, printed p.388; agent expansion to arbitrary finite simplicial shapes and the stated path-fiber orientation.

proof.text: Form the relative undercategory $C_b$ and its projection $U$ of [lem-coef-relative-undercategory-limit-creation]; it is the comma quasicategory of [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback] for the cospan $\Delta^0\xrightarrow{b}B\xleftarrow{G}A$. There is a degreewise inclusion $Q_b\subseteq C_b$: forget that the $A$-simplices and the whole arrow prism in $B$ lie in the cores. Let $K$ be finite, possibly empty, and let $g:K\to Q_b$ be any map. Regard it as $d:K\to C_b$. The diagram $Ud$ has a limit in $A$ by hypothesis. Its image under $G$ is a limit cone by limit preservation. The cited relative-undercategory lemma therefore supplies a limiting cone $\lambda:\Delta_Kc\to d$ in $C_b$, with $c=(a,\psi:b\to G(a))$. No contractibility of $K$ is used.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, proof, printed p.388; agent expansion to arbitrary finite simplicial shapes and the stated path-fiber orientation.

proof.text: Right approximation applied to $\psi$ gives $v:a'\to a$ and an equivalence $e:b\to G(a')$ with $[G(v)e]=[\psi]$. Put $c'=(a',e)\in C_b$. The mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback] for this cospan, whose $\Delta^0$-factor $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^0}(*,*)$ is a point, identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{C_b}(c',c)$, compatibly with $U$, with the homotopy fiber over $\psi$ of $\operatorname{Map}_A(a',a)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(b,G(a))$, $v\mapsto G(v)e$. This fiber is nonempty: the vertex $v$ and a path from its composite class to $\psi$ give a point of the stated homotopy fiber. Equality in $\pi_0$ gives such a path, since the mapping spaces are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; a finite zigzag can be reversed and composed by filling two-dimensional horns. The natural equivalence of mapping spaces is surjective on components, so it gives an edge $w:c'\to c$. Its projected class is $[v]$. Thus an equality only in $hB$ has been used to obtain coherent comma data, rather than being treated as a strict triangle.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, proof, printed p.388; agent expansion to arbitrary finite simplicial shapes and the stated path-fiber orientation.

proof.text: Since $C_b$ is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback], $\operatorname{Fun}(K,C_b)$ is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Its two composable edges $\Delta_Kw$ and $\lambda$ fill an inner two-horn, giving an edge $h:\Delta_Kc'\to d$. By definition [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], this is an actual map $H:K\times\Delta^1\to C_b$, with endpoints exactly the constant map at $c'$ and $d$. The inner-horn filler also retains the compatibility with the original limiting cone; no passage to the homotopy category of diagrams is being substituted for this map.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, proof, printed p.388; agent expansion to arbitrary finite simplicial shapes and the stated path-fiber orientation.

proof.text: At a vertex $k\in K$, write $d(k)=(a_k,e_k:b\to G(a_k))$ and $t_k=U(h_k):a'\to a_k$. The coherent square defining the edge $h_k$ in $C_b$ yields $[G(t_k)][e]=[e_k]$ in $hB$; its two triangular faces give this equation by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Both $e$ and $e_k$ are equivalences, so $[G(t_k)]=[e_k][e]^{-1}$ is invertible. The same cited lemma identifies invertible component classes with equivalence edges. Conservativity of $G$ now makes every $t_k$ an equivalence in $A$. This step uses conservativity only on these component edges.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, proof, printed p.388; agent expansion to arbitrary finite simplicial shapes and the stated path-fiber orientation.

proof.text: The endpoints of $UH$ carry all edges of $K$ to equivalences, since they are a constant diagram and the $A^\simeq$-coordinate of $g$. The vertical edges $t_k$ are equivalences by step 5. Every remaining diagonal edge of $K\times\Delta^1$ is the composite, up to a triangular face, of a horizontal and a vertical edge; [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] therefore makes it an equivalence as well. Thus $UH$ factors through $A^\simeq$. The $B$-coordinate of $H$ is a map $K\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to B$, whose last interval is the comma arrow. Its layer at 0 is constantly $b$, its layer at 1 is $GUH$, and its transverse edges are $e$ or an $e_k$. All these edges are equivalences. An arbitrary diagonal edge of the triple product is a composite of these coordinate edges, witnessed by the triangular faces of its parameter cube, so is an equivalence by the same composition criterion. Hence this entire map factors through $B^\simeq$. The pullback equations remain exact, and $H$ factors degreewise through $Q_b$. It contracts $g$ to $q=c'$. For $K=\varnothing$, the limit in step 2 is the empty limit and step 3 still supplies the vertex $q$; steps about edges are vacuous.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, proof, printed p.388; agent expansion to arbitrary finite simplicial shapes and the stated path-fiber orientation.

proof.text: For the original $f:K\to P_b$, apply steps 2-6 to $g=Rf$. Postcomposing its homotopy with $S$ gives a homotopy from the constant map at $p=S(q)$ to $SRf$. The homotopy $SR\simeq\operatorname{id}_{P_b}$ of [lem-coef-kan-fiber-path-reversal], restricted along $f$, joins $SRf$ to $f$. By [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance], $\operatorname{Fun}(K,P_b)$ is Kan (apply its assertion with the identity weak equivalence of $K$). Reverse either of these edges if necessary by an outer two-horn, then compose them by an inner two-horn. The resulting single edge is precisely a simplicial homotopy $K\times\Delta^1\to P_b$ with the required endpoints. Taking the unique map from the empty simplicial set yields a vertex $p\in P_b$ and the required empty homotopy.

lean.statement: theorem finite_core_fiber_contraction (A B : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory A] [Quasicategory B] (hA : SuspensionComparison.HasFiniteLimits A) (hB : SuspensionComparison.HasFiniteLimits B) (G : A ⟶ B) (hG : ∀ (K : SSet.{u}), K.Finite → PreservesLimitsOfShape G K) (hReflects : ∀ (v : A _⦋1⦌), IsEquivalenceEdge B (G.app _ v) → IsEquivalenceEdge A v) (hApprox : ∀ (a : A _⦋0⦌) (b : B _⦋0⦌) (ψ : (mappingSpace B b (G.app _ a)) _⦋0⦌), ∃ (a' : A _⦋0⦌) (v : (mappingSpace A a' a) _⦋0⦌) (e : (mappingSpace B b (G.app _ a')) _⦋0⦌) (w : (mappingSpace B b (G.app _ a)) _⦋0⦌) (t : B _⦋2⦌), IsEquivalenceEdge B e.val ∧ B.δ 2 t = e.val ∧ B.δ 0 t = G.app _ v.val ∧ B.δ 1 t = w.val ∧ π₀.mk w = π₀.mk ψ) : ∀ (b : (core B).toSSet _⦋0⦌), Nonempty ((homotopyFiber (coreMap G) b) _⦋0⦌) ∧ ∀ (K : SSet.{u}) [K.Finite] (f : K ⟶ homotopyFiber (coreMap G) b), ∃ p : (homotopyFiber (coreMap G) b) _⦋0⦌, Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (SSet.const p) f)
lean.note: Uses existing finite coherent limits, actual cone preservation and coreMap. Right approximation is equality in pi_0 of the specified mapping space; a two-simplex witnesses composition without requiring a strict triangle to the given psi.
